tagline: Called in on his day off. Stayed for dinner.

    StartersPerfect dozen devilled eggsTwelve devilled eggs with Dijon, paprika and chivesHow to make it6 eggs3 tbsp mayonnaise1 tsp Dijon mustard1 tsp white vinegarsmoked paprika, to dust1 tbsp chopped chivesBoil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and halve.Mash the yolks with the mayonnaise, Dijon and vinegar.Pipe the filling back into the whites, dust with paprika and add chives. Exactly twelve.Quick Stop chips with nacho cheeseChips with hot cheddar cheese sauce and pickled jalapeñosHow to make it20g butter1 tbsp plain flour300ml milk200g cheddar, grated2 tbsp chopped pickled jalapenos1 tbsp jalapeno pickling liquid1/2 tsp smoked paprika300g corn chipsMelt the butter, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Whisk in the milk and simmer until thick.Off the heat, stir in the cheddar until smooth, then the jalapenos, pickling liquid and paprika.Warm the corn chips on a tray at 180°C for 4 minutes. Serve with the hot cheese for dunking.Rooftop hockey soft pretzelsThe hockey game on the store roofHow to make itAs written, serves 4Soft pretzel knots dipped in bicarb water, sprinkled with rock salt and baked deep brown, served warm with a sharp two-mustard dip.Mix 400g plain flour, 7g dried yeast, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp salt and 250ml warm water, knead 8 minutes and prove 1 hour.Divide into 8, roll into ropes and tie into knots.Dip each in 2L boiling water with 60g bicarb soda for 30 seconds.Sprinkle with rock salt and bake at 220°C for 12 minutes.Serve with wholegrain mustard and a little hot English mustard mixed together.Smoked beef jerky sticksRandal rings it up, then eats half.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsJersey hoagieSalami, ham and provolone with lettuce, tomato, onion, oil and red wine vinegarHow to make it4 long bread rolls150g salami, sliced150g leg ham, sliced100g provolone, sliced1/4 iceberg lettuce, shredded2 tomatoes, sliced1 onion, thinly sliced2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil2 tbsp red wine vinegar1 tsp dried oreganoSplit the rolls and layer with the salami, ham, provolone, lettuce, tomato and onion.Drizzle with oil and vinegar and sprinkle with oregano. Wrap tight and cut in half.Veronica's ricotta beef lasagneThe lasagne Veronica brings to the storeHow to make itAs written, serves 4Beef ragù simmered slowly with tomato and red wine, layered with lasagne sheets, lemony ricotta and mozzarella, baked bubbling and rested before cutting.Brown 800g beef mince with an onion and 3 garlic cloves.Add 150ml red wine, 2 cans crushed tomatoes and oregano and simmer 2 hours.Mix 500g ricotta with an egg, 50g parmesan, lemon zest and parsley.In a dish, layer ragù, 300g lasagne sheets and ricotta three times, finishing with ragù and 250g mozzarella.Bake at 180°C for 45 minutes and rest 20 minutes before cutting.SweetsQuick Stop cream-filled chocolate cakesChocolate sponge rectangles sandwiched with marshmallow buttercreamHow to make it3 eggs100g caster sugar70g self-raising flour20g cocoa100g butter, soft200g icing sugar100g marshmallow fluff1 tsp vanilla extract150g dark chocolate50ml thickened creamWhisk the eggs and caster sugar until thick, then fold in the flour and cocoa.Spread in a lined slice tin and bake at 180°C for 12 minutes. Cool and cut into 12 rectangles.Beat the butter, most of the icing sugar, marshmallow fluff and vanilla until fluffy. Sandwich pairs of cake with it.Melt the chocolate with the cream and dip the cakes in it. Let them set.Mix the leftover icing sugar with a few drops of water and pipe a white squiggle on top.DrinksBack fridge chocolate malt shakeChocolate malted milkshake with vanilla ice cream and crushed malt ballsHow to make it600ml cold milk1 L vanilla ice cream2 tbsp cocoa4 tbsp malted milk powder1 cup chocolate malt ballsBlend the milk, ice cream, cocoa and malt powder until thick and frothy.Crush the malt balls in a bag with a rolling pin.Pour into four chilled tall glasses, scatter the crushed malt balls over and add a straw.Frozen CokeI'm not even supposed to be here today.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
